title: In-person meetings
lead: Is lesson ke baad tum client ko office me welcome kar sakte ho, demo dikha sakte ho, price aur offer bata sakte ho, aur politely goodbye bol sakte ho.
description: Week 8 English lesson: welcome a client, give an office tour, show a demo, make an offer, and end a meeting politely.

patterns.note: Pehli mulaqat par fixed phrase. End me: Nice meeting you.
patterns.negative: It's not our first meeting — we spoke on Zoom.
patterns.question: Is this your first visit to our office?
examples: Nice to meet you. Thank you for coming.
Aapse mil kar achha laga. Aane ke liye thanks.
It's nice to meet you too.
Aap se milkar bhi achha laga.
patterns.grammar: Nice to meet you = pehli mulaqat. Meeting ke end me Nice meeting you. Response: Nice to meet you too.
patterns.mistake: “Nice to meet to you” → “Nice to meet you.” meet ke baad to nahi.

patterns.note: Office, demo ya product dikhane ka offer.
patterns.say: Let me show you our office.
patterns.positive: Let me show you our office.
patterns.negative: I can't show you the server room.
patterns.question: Can you show me the design?
examples: Let me show you the demo.
Main aapko demo dikhata hoon.
Let me show you our new office.
Main aapko hamara naya office dikhata hoon.
patterns.grammar: Let me + base verb + object. show someone something.
patterns.mistake: “Let me to show you” → “Let me show you.” let me ke baad base verb.

patterns.note: Polite offer — chai, paani, seat ya demo.
patterns.negative: No, thank you. I don't want anything right now.
patterns.question: Would you like to see the demo?
examples: Would you like some water?
Kya aap paani lena chahenge?
Would you like to sit down?
Kya aap baithna chahenge?
patterns.grammar: Would you like + noun / to + verb. Polite offer. Answer: Yes, please. / No, thank you.
patterns.mistake: “Do you like some water?” (offer) → “Would you like some water?” Offer ke liye would.

patterns.note: Price, discount ya package batane ke liye.
patterns.say: We can offer a ten percent discount.
patterns.positive: We can offer a ten percent discount.
patterns.question: What can you offer?
examples: We can offer a monthly plan.
Hum monthly plan de sakte hain.
We can offer two designs.
Hum do designs de sakte hain.
patterns.grammar: can offer + noun. Negotiation me range batao, promise zyada mat karo.
patterns.mistake: “We can offer to you a discount” → “We can offer you a discount.” offer + person + thing.

patterns.note: Kuch dete time — card, list, sample.
patterns.question: Is this the final price?
examples: Here is my card.
Ye mera card hai.
Here are the samples.
Ye samples hain.
patterns.grammar: Here is + singular; Here are + plural. Handing something over.
patterns.mistake: “Here is our samples” → “Here are our samples.” Plural ke liye here are.

patterns.note: Client ki opinion poochho — meeting ko interactive banao.
patterns.say: What do you think about the design?
patterns.positive: What do you think about the design?
patterns.negative: I'm not sure what you think.
patterns.question: What do you think?
examples: What do you think of the new homepage?
Naye homepage ke baare me kya sochte hain?
What do you think? Should we change the colour?
Aap kya sochte hain? Colour badlein?
patterns.grammar: What do you think of/about + noun? Think ke baad opinion. Alone bhi chalega.
patterns.mistake: “What do you think about?” → “What do you think?” ya “What do you think about it?”

dialogue.context: Client office visit. Riya = client. Welcome, tour, demo, offer aur goodbye — sab cover karo.

lines.speaker: Riya
lines.text: Hello! We have a meeting at eleven.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Welcome. Nice to meet you. Let me show you our office first.

lines.speaker: Riya
lines.text: Thank you. The office looks nice.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Would you like some tea before the demo?

lines.speaker: Riya
lines.text: Yes, please. And what is the price?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Here is our price list. We can offer you a ten percent discount for the first year.

lines.speaker: Riya
lines.text: That sounds good. What do you think about the timeline?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: I think two weeks is realistic. I'll send you the final quote by Monday.

dialogue.closing: In-person meeting me chai, demo, price aur next step — chaar moments. Har moment ke liye ek line yaad rakho.

speakPrompts.title: 1. Welcome
speakPrompts.prompt: Client ko office me welcome karo.
speakPrompts.starter: Welcome. Nice to meet you. Let me show you ___ .

speakPrompts.title: 2. Offer something
speakPrompts.starter: Would you like ___ ? Yes, please. / No, thank you.

speakPrompts.title: 3. Show and ask
speakPrompts.starter: Let me show you ___ . What do you think about ___ ?

speakPrompts.title: 4. Price and goodbye
speakPrompts.prompt: Price batao aur meeting close karo.
speakPrompts.starter: Here is ___ . We can offer ___ . I'll send you ___ by ___ .

selfCheck: Client ko “Nice to meet you” se welcome kiya.
Office ya demo “Let me show you ___” se dikhaya.
Price ya package “We can offer ___” se bataya.
Ek opinion poochhi — “What do you think?”
Next step aur goodbye clear tha.

pronunciation.title: Polite intonation
pronunciation.body: Would you LIKE some TEA? — voice end me soft up. Demand nahi, offer lagta hai.

pronunciation.title: Prices
pronunciation.body: ten percent = /ten pəˈsent/. Fifteen vs fifty: fifTEEN (stress end), FIFty (stress start).

pronunciation.title: Linking
pronunciation.body: meet you → /miːtʃuː/; would you → /wʊdʒə/. In-person me bhi natural linking chahiye.

pronunciation.title: Numbers
pronunciation.body: 1,500 = fifteen hundred; 15,000 = fifteen thousand. Lakh/crore ko client ke saath clear karo.
